summary: This is Snowflake's reference page for the CREATE CONNECTION SQL command, which creates a connection in an account and requires Business Critical Edition or higher. It gives the syntax for a primary connection and a secondary (replica) connection, the name rules, the optional COMMENT parameter, and the access requirement that only ACCOUNTADMIN users can run it. Two examples show creating a connection for account myaccount1 in organization myorg and creating a replica of that primary connection.
one_line: Snowflake reference for the CREATE CONNECTION command, which creates primary or replica connections for account failover and redirection.
key_facts: CREATE CONNECTION requires Business Critical Edition (or higher).
Creates a new connection in the account.
The name must start with an alphabetic character and may only contain letters, decimal digits (0-9), and underscores (_).
For a primary connection, the name must be unique across connection names and account names in the organization.
For a secondary connection, the name must match the name of its primary connection.
The AS REPLICA OF clause specifies the primary connection as organization_name.account_name.name.
The COMMENT parameter is optional and defaults to no value.
Only account administrators (users with the ACCOUNTADMIN role) can execute this SQL command.
Customers should ensure no personal data (other than for a User object), sensitive data, export-controlled data, or other regulated data is entered as metadata.
The syntax for creating a primary connection is CREATE CONNECTION [ IF NOT EXISTS ] <name> [ COMMENT = '<string_literal>' ].
Example: CREATE CONNECTION IF NOT EXISTS myconnection; creates a connection for account myaccount1 in organization myorg.
Example: CREATE CONNECTION myconnection AS REPLICA OF myorg.myaccount1.myconnection; creates a secondary connection as a replica of its primary connection.
The page is listed under Replication, Failover/Failback, and Client Redirect topics.
